interaction.text:
The balled-up sheet of paper the maid slipped you back at the Guild Hall, smoothed flat and reread for the tenth time. "One of the guards was scribbling this the night it happened. Chucked it in the bin when his sergeant told him to redo it properly, he'd spelled everything wrong. I fished it back out. Don't tell them I still have it." In a cramped hand:

vict. consc + orientatd most of the night, talkin fine til near the end

compl. of pins-n-needles in lips + fingers, then hands gone cold n sweaty

queezy, said stumach felt wrong, no actual sicking up tho

pulse raisd, gone iregular by the time the physiscian arived

collapsd sudden, quick after that

(pupils - not noted. sarge says i missed it. redo this properly. - ed.)

Whatever happened, it happened fast, and whoever did it knew exactly what they were doing.

_incomplete: Converted from herbalist_Interior.tmj/tmx (INFINITE/CHUNKED Tiled format), merged all chunks into a dense 32x32 grid with computed origin offset (tile-space [-16, -16]). Collision built from the authored 'walkable area' polygon (rasterized), not from Walls/floor tile footprints. The front 'entrance/exit' rect already landed on a walkable tile from the polygon, no carving needed there. The 'back door' rect sat entirely outside the walkable polygon (same pattern as the manor/barn/dock door-threshold fixes earlier in this project) so its own footprint was carved open directly: tiles [(20, 12), (21, 12), (20, 13), (21, 13), (20, 14), (21, 14)]. IMPORTANT: this back door is NOT wired to a zone_exit or anything else, on purpose, matching the project's standing lesson about not pointing an exit at a placeholder target that would silently do nothing. Where it leads (further into the swamp? a second room?) is an open design question, not yet asked. npc_herbalist and prop_cauldron are both placeholder flavor-only 'note' objects, not real content or a real mechanic. The actual Herbalist NPC sprite (idle+walk, 32px cell, matches the project's standard look-manifest shape) exists in the CraftPix pack and has been wired into public/assets/npcs/looks/manifest.json as look id 'herbalist', but npc_herbalist here still uses a plain map-marker position rather than that look, since giving her a name/identity/dialogue before the act's design is confirmed risks writing content that gets thrown away. Whoever builds this act next should swap npc_herbalist to use the 'herbalist' look and replace both placeholder notes with real interactions once the plant-matching mechanic itself is designed.
